title: Guided Meditation Mix
desc:
I have a clean, spoken-word meditation that needs to flow effortlessly over a single, music that needs to be looped. 

 I will supply the raw voice file, the backing track, and time-stamp notes on where the music should start, dip, or fade.  

Your job is to edit, clean, and professionally mix the two elements so the guidance remains clearly on top of the music at every moment, with subtle volume automation keeping the vocal dominant yet warm. Please take care of basic noise reduction, gentle EQ, tasteful reverb that matches the “other-worldly” mood, and smooth transitions that hide any edits.  

When you’re done, deliver a lossless WAV (48 kHz/24-bit) and an MP3, plus the session or stems in case I need future tweaks. If anything in my timing notes feels off once you hear the takes, flag it and suggest a smoother alternative—I’m happy to adjust to achieve a coherent, transportive final piece.

title: Spiral Tube Heat Exchanger with varying pitch, with ribbed Optimization with grid independence test, report and thesis, graphs
desc:
I am completing an M.Tech thesis centred on a spiral-tube heat exchanger and I need a professional design-and-analysis package that I can defend academically. The exchanger must achieve three simultaneous goals: higher heat-transfer efficiency, lower pressure drop, and a compact footprint.  

The model has to treat water loaded with Al₂O₃ nanoparticles as the working fluid, so please include its temperature-dependent properties throughout the calculations.

Scope of work  
• Build a 3-D CAD model of the spiral-tube heat exchanger, specifying all key dimensions, materials, coil pitch and baffles.  
• Run CFD (ANSYS Fluent, COMSOL Multiphysics, or an equivalent solver you are comfortable with) to predict temperature fields, overall heat-transfer coefficient and pressure drop.  
• Optimise the geometry iteratively until the best balance of efficiency, pressure loss and size is reached.  
• Document the procedure in a concise report with contour plots, tables, and comparison to a straight-tube baseline.  
• Hand over editable CAD files, simulation files, and the final report in Word/PDF.

Acceptance criteria  
The final design must demonstrate at least a 15 % improvement in heat-transfer coefficient over the baseline, keep pressure drop under the limit I will share after award, and fit within the lab rig envelope I will provide.
